expectations.title: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems
expectations.description: Interpret products and quotients of whole numbers through equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.

expectations.title: Understand fractions as numbers built from unit fractions
expectations.description: Understand 1/b as one equal part of a whole and build fractions a/b from a copies of 1/b.

expectations.title: Relate area to multiplication and addition
expectations.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement using unit squares.

skills.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
skills.description: Interpret products as equal groups and arrays.

canonical.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
canonical.description: Understand multiplication as equal groups, arrays, and repeated addition.

problems.prompt: There are 3 rows with 4 counters in each row. How many counters are there?
problems.objective: Diagnose whether the learner interprets an array as equal groups.

problems.prompt: Five bags each hold 2 marbles. How many marbles are in all?
problems.objective: Guide the learner from a context to an equal-groups product.

problems.prompt: What product is represented by 4 equal groups of 6?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of equal-groups interpretation.

problems.prompt: A garden has 7 short rows with 3 plants in each row. How many plants are there?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of equal-groups multiplication in context.

skills.name: Division as Equal Sharing
skills.description: Interpret quotients through fair sharing and groups of a known size.

canonical.name: Division as Equal Sharing
canonical.description: Understand division as fair sharing and as finding an unknown group size or number of groups.

problems.prompt: Twelve counters are shared equally among 3 children. How many counters does each child get?
Eighteen shells are placed into groups of 6. How many groups are made?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to interpret quotative division.

problems.prompt: Twenty-four pencils are packed equally into 4 boxes. How many pencils go in each box?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of equal-sharing division.

problems.prompt: A coach places 28 cones in rows of 7. How many rows are made?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of equal-sharing division in context.

skills.name: Unit Fractions as Numbers
skills.description: Understand 1/b as one equal part of a whole and build fractions from it.

canonical.name: Unit Fractions as Numbers
canonical.description: Understand unit fractions 1/b and build non-unit fractions a/b from unit fractions.

problems.prompt: A strip is divided into 4 equal parts. What fraction is one part?
problems.objective: Diagnose understanding of 1/b as one equal part.

problems.prompt: One equal part of a whole is 1/6. How many equal parts make the whole?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to connect unit fractions to the whole.

problems.prompt: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal spaces. What fraction names the first mark after 0?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of unit fractions on a number line.

problems.prompt: Mina uses 3 pieces of size 1/5. What fraction of the whole does she have?
problems.objective: Verify mastery of building non-unit fractions from unit fractions.

skills.name: Rectangle Area with Unit Squares
skills.description: Relate rectangular arrays, unit squares, and multiplication to area.

canonical.name: Rectangle Area with Unit Squares
canonical.description: Understand area as covering with unit squares and relate it to multiplication.

problems.prompt: A rectangle has 3 rows of 5 unit squares. What is its area in square units?
problems.objective: Diagnose understanding of area as rows of unit squares.

problems.prompt: A rectangular mat is 4 units long and 2 units wide. What is its area?
problems.objective: Guide the learner to multiply length and width for area.

problems.prompt: A rectangle covers 6 rows with 3 unit squares in each row. What area does it cover?
problems.objective: Collect independent evidence of rectangle area reasoning.

problems.prompt: A board is 7 units by 4 units. Find its area in square units.
problems.objective: Verify mastery of rectangle area with unit squares.
